providers.intro: Folio gets its data from these sources. Switch a source off and Folio stops asking it, whatever the reason: you do not trust it, you want to save its daily calls, or you are testing. A source that needs a key (see below) is skipped until you save one.

what.eodhd: Closing prices, delayed quotes and news, and fund holdings on paid plans. Needs a key. The free plan allows 20 calls a day.
what.yahoo: Free closing prices and quotes without a key. It is an unofficial source, used as the main or backup price source.
what.twelvedata: A backup source for prices. Needs a key (a free plan exists).
what.openfigi: Finds the fund and its exchanges from an ISIN when you add an instrument. Works without a key; a free key allows more lookups.
what.ecb: The euro exchange rates and the deposit rate. Switching it off means holdings priced in other currencies cannot be turned into euro.
what.fred: US economic series for the Macro page and strategy rules. Needs a free key.

providers.keysHint: Keys are stored encrypted and never shown again in full. {{names}} need one to be used.
providers.advanced: Advanced: priority and daily call limit
providers.advancedHint: For each source: priority (1 is asked first; the next one is tried when it fails) and the daily call limit (0 uses the usual limit). The on/off switches above write the same setting.
